official.deadline_note: No fixed calendar deadline is published for either component. The Early Bird discount runs on a relative deadline: the applicant must accept the study offer and pay the tuition fee within 28 days after the admission decisions have been published, and for 2026 the final date to accept and pay was 24 April. The Merit Scholarship has a separate application process: 'The admission services of the University will invite all eligible applicants to apply for the scholarship when the application round opens in spring.'
official.application_cycle: Merit Scholarship: annual spring application round, by invitation from admission services, for the following academic year. Early Bird discount: automatic at each admission decision.
official.status_note: Neither component is open at the time of checking. The University states that scholarships are not available to first-year students, so there are no scholarship requirements in the admission process; the Merit Scholarship round opens in spring by invitation, and the Early Bird discount is triggered at the point of admission.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The University states: 'It is not possible to get a scholarship to cover the tuition fee for the first year, but the University offers an Early Bird discount of 2,000 EUR for master's degree applicants' and that all students who fulfil the requirements are eligible for 'a scholarship that covers 50% of the tuition fee for the next study year'. Turku's programmes charge either EUR 10,000 or EUR 12,000 per academic year depending on the programme.

official.description: Since the 2026 intake the University of Turku no longer funds a first year of tuition. Instead it offers an automatic 2,000 EUR Early Bird discount to newly admitted master's students who accept and pay quickly, and a Merit Scholarship covering 50% of the tuition fee for the following study year to students who have already paid for their first year at Turku and met credit, grade and Finnish language thresholds.

applicant_utility.summary: Read this as two different awards on one page. The Early Bird discount is pure timing: accept the offer and pay within 28 days of the admission decision and 2,000 EUR comes off automatically, with no application, no essay and no competition. The Merit Scholarship is a reward you earn only after you have already paid a full year of tuition at Turku, so it is a discount for continuing students rather than a way into the country. If you need money for year one, this programme has none to give, and the honest plan is external funding for the first year plus Turku's 50% for year two.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fee-paying master's applicants who can pay a full first year quickly, and continuing Turku students with 55 credits, a 3.0 average and 4 credits of Finnish.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up the full first-year tuition fee before the admission decisions are published, because the 28-day Early Bird window is unforgiving and requires payment in a single instalment
Plan your first-year credit load to clear 55 ECTS, since that is the single gate that decides the second-year award
Book at least 4 credits of Finnish in your first year; these can be counted inside the 55-credit requirement, so they are effectively free progress
Watch your grade average against the 3.0 threshold on the 1-5 scale rather than assuming an honours-level mark is what is meant
Keep your contact details current with admission services, because the Merit Scholarship application is by invitation only and there is no open portal to stumble into
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 28-day payment window and losing the 2,000 EUR discount, which the university had to correct publicly from 30 days to 28 days
Assuming the discount applies to bachelor's programmes; it does not
Believing a first-year scholarship exists; since the 2026 intake no Turku scholarship can cover first-year tuition
Finishing the first year with fewer than 55 credits, which ends the Merit Scholarship for the following year
Missing the spring invitation because the application is not open continuously
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The full first-year tuition fee, since no Turku scholarship covers it, plus 50% of the tuition in any year not covered by the Merit Scholarship, plus living costs of roughly 600-900 EUR per month in Turku, the Student Union membership fee of around EUR 55 per academic year and the compulsory Student Health Care fee paid to Kela.
document_audit: There is no Merit Scholarship document checklist published; the application comes to you by invitation, so the instructions travel with that invitation
For the Early Bird discount the only real document trap is the payment itself: the discounted fee must be paid as one instalment, and it is the payment status, not the acceptance, that counts
If your programme's fee is unusually low, note that the pre-2026 rules excluded double-degree programmes with tuition under EUR 3,000; confirm your current programme's treatment with admissions

Students admitted in 2025 or before follow entirely different rules, including full-tuition two- and three-year scholarships, so check which regime your admission year falls under before relying on any figure
alerts: The scholarship system changed fundamentally for the 2026 intake, so any listing describing generous two- or three-year full-tuition Turku scholarships is describing the pre-2026 scheme
The 28-day Early Bird window was previously misstated as 30 days on the university's own site, so verify the exact date stated in your admission letter rather than a general rule
The Merit Scholarship is not competitive, which is genuinely good news: if you meet the thresholds you are awarded, so the risk is failing a threshold rather than losing a ranking contest
Do not confuse this with the Fulbright-University of Turku Graduate Award, which is a different award for US citizens with a 1,000 EUR per month grant plus tuition
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: No scholarship application at admission; the Early Bird discount is automatic on acceptance and payment within 28 days, and the Merit Scholarship application follows a spring invitation from admission services after the first study year is complete.
